cases.sentence: ___ пытался сына спасти, сам его прооперировал, но ребенок все равно умер
cases.translation: The professor tried to save his son, operated on him himself, but the child died anyway.
cases.explain: Профессор is the subject of the verb пытался (tried), so it stands in the Nominative case.

cases.sentence: Я вообще временно стал очень сентиментален после ___
cases.translation: I temporarily became very sentimental after the poisoning.
cases.explain: The preposition после ("after") governs the Genitive case, so отравление becomes отравления.

cases.sentence: Вставать мне не разрешали долго, потому что я был склонен к ___
cases.translation: I wasn't allowed to stand up for a long time, because I was prone to trying to escape.
cases.explain: The preposition к ("toward/prone to") governs the Dative case, so побег becomes побегу.

cases.sentence: В ночь подсчета голосов я заставляю ___ читать мне твиттер вслух
cases.translation: On the night of the vote count, I make Yulia read Twitter to me aloud.
cases.explain: Юля is the direct object of заставляю (I make/force), so it takes the Accusative case.

cases.sentence: Она давала ложку, и этой ___ нужно было зачерпнуть воду из полной чашки
cases.translation: She gave me a spoon, and with that spoon I had to scoop water from the full cup.
cases.explain: The Instrumental expresses the tool used for the action ("with the spoon"), so ложка becomes ложкой.

cases.sentence: Они рассказывали мне про больницу в ___, наполненную ФСБшниками
cases.translation: They told me about the hospital in Omsk, full of FSB agents.
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating location governs the Prepositional case, so Омск becomes Омске.

cases.sentence: И тут мне дают ___ и просят, напиши что-нибудь
cases.translation: And then they hand me a pencil and ask me to write something.
cases.explain: Карандаш is the direct object of дают (they give), so it takes the Accusative case.

cases.sentence: Когда она уже после ___ показала мне эту бумажку, оказалось, что там не текст
cases.translation: When she showed me that piece of paper after my discharge, it turned out there was no text on it.
cases.explain: The preposition после ("after") governs the Genitive case, so выписка becomes выписки.

reading.ru: Если вы думаете, что пробуждение из комы — дело одной секунды, как в кино, то я вас разочарую.
reading.question: What does Navalny say about waking up from a coma?
options: It's not instantaneous like in the movies
It happened exactly like in the movies
He remembers nothing about it at all
It was completely painless and quick
reading.correct: It's not instantaneous like in the movies
reading.explain: He opens the chapter warning that waking from a coma is not "дело одной секунды, как в кино".

reading.ru: Я умер и очутился в мире галлюцинаций.
reading.question: What did Navalny experience after "dying"?
options: A vivid dream of his childhood
reading.correct: A world of hallucinations
reading.explain: He writes "Я умер и очутился в мире галлюцинаций" (I died and found myself in a world of hallucinations).

reading.ru: Вот кто-то бреет мне лицо.
reading.question: What is one fragment Navalny recalls from his first days regaining consciousness?
reading.correct: Someone shaving his face
reading.explain: Among his scattered memories he recalls "кто-то бреет мне лицо".

reading.ru: Но проблема была не в том, что я не мог говорить, а в том, что я не мог придумать слово.
reading.question: What was Navalny's core problem when a doctor asked him to say a word?
options: He couldn't think of any word to say
He was physically unable to speak
He refused to cooperate with doctors
reading.correct: He couldn't think of any word to say
reading.explain: He explains the issue was that "я не мог придумать слово" (he couldn't think of a word).

reading.ru: Чаще других меня навещал мой лечащий врач, профессор, очень известный и уважаемый нейрохирург из Японии.
reading.question: Who did Navalny believe was his most frequent visitor and doctor?
reading.correct: A famous Japanese neurosurgeon
reading.explain: He recalls being visited most often by "нейрохирург из Японии".

reading.ru: у него, оказывается, совсем недавно трагически погиб двухлетний сын.
reading.question: What tragedy did Navalny believe had befallen the Japanese professor?
options: He had lost his medical license
reading.correct: His two-year-old son had died
reading.explain: Nurses supposedly told him the professor's "двухлетний сын" had recently died tragically.

reading.ru: Можете представить себе мое разочарование, когда мне сказали, что никакого японского профессора не существует.
reading.question: What did Navalny eventually learn about the Japanese professor?
options: He never existed — it was a hallucination
He had been transferred to another hospital
He had been arrested by police
reading.correct: He never existed — it was a hallucination
reading.explain: He was told "что никакого японского профессора не существует".

reading.ru: Я не помню, как впервые после комы увидел свою жену.
reading.question: Does Navalny remember the first time he saw his wife after the coma?
options: No, there was no single such moment he recalls
He saw her before he woke up
He mistook her for a nurse at first
reading.correct: No, there was no single such moment he recalls
reading.explain: He states plainly "Я не помню, как впервые после комы увидел свою жену".

reading.ru: в какой-то момент вдруг понял, что там нарисованы сердечки.
reading.question: What did Navalny eventually realize was drawn on the board across from his hospital bed?
options: Little hearts, drawn daily by Yulia
reading.correct: Little hearts, drawn daily by Yulia
reading.explain: Staring at the board, he "вдруг понял, что там нарисованы сердечки", drawn by Yulia each day.

reading.ru: в сердцах написал вдруг возникшее в моем подсознании слово «фак».
reading.question: What word did Navalny angrily scrawl when he couldn't remember how to spell "water" in English?
reading.correct: "Fuck"
reading.explain: In frustration he "в сердцах написал ... слово «фак»".

reading.ru: Я сижу в тюремной камере на шконке.
reading.question: What did Navalny hallucinate about involving a Russian rap group's lyrics?
options: Being imprisoned and forced to recite the group Krovostok's lyrics
Performing a concert with the group
reading.correct: Being imprisoned and forced to recite the group Krovostok's lyrics
reading.explain: He dreamed he was in a prison cell where guards forced him to recite the lyrics of the rap group «Кровосток».

reading.ru: Однажды они решили включить мне футбол.
reading.question: Why did Leonid Volkov intervene when the staff turned on the TV?
options: Because Navalny didn't actually like football
Because the game was too loud
Because it was in a foreign language
reading.correct: Because Navalny didn't actually like football
reading.explain: Leonid objected, saying "Вы зачем футбол ему включаете? Он его не любит!" after staff turned on football.

reading.ru: я вдруг посмотрел прямо на них и сказал, «Блядь, что? Ведь это же так тупо».
reading.question: What word triggered the breakthrough moment when Navalny first reacted lucidly?
reading.correct: "Novichok" (the poison's name)
reading.explain: When they said the word «новичок», he suddenly looked at them and reacted lucidly.

reading.ru: В Томске победили 19 из 27 поддержанных нами кандидатов
reading.question: How many of the 27 supported candidates won in Tomsk?
reading.explain: The results state "В Томске победили 19 из 27 поддержанных нами кандидатов".

reading.ru: В Новосибирске депутатами стали 12 кандидатов, которых мы поддержали
reading.question: How many supported candidates became deputies in Novosibirsk?
reading.explain: The text states "В Новосибирске депутатами стали 12 кандидатов, которых мы поддержали".

reading.ru: Оставшись один, я сорвал с себя катетеры и трубки, залив палату кровью и попытался встать.
reading.question: What did Navalny do when left alone in his hospital room?
options: He tore off his catheters and tubes trying to get up
He wrote a letter to Putin
reading.correct: He tore off his catheters and tubes trying to get up
reading.explain: Left alone, "я сорвал с себя катетеры и трубки, залив палату кровью и попытался встать".

reading.ru: Я боялся, что это навсегда.
reading.question: What fear gripped Navalny after struggling to walk just a few steps to the sink?
options: That his weakness would be permanent
That he would be arrested again
That his wife would leave him
That he would lose his job
reading.correct: That his weakness would be permanent
reading.explain: He recalls the terror that "я боялся, что это навсегда".

reading.ru: Ко мне каждый день приходил физиотерапевт.
reading.question: What difficult exercise did the physiotherapist have Navalny practice?
options: Transferring water between cups with a spoon
reading.correct: Transferring water between cups with a spoon
reading.explain: The physiotherapist made him scoop water from one cup to another with a spoon, counted as spoonfuls.

reading.ru: Наверное, самым классным в реанимации был тот день, когда из Москвы наконец прилетели наши дети, Даша и Захар.
reading.question: What was one of the best days for Navalny in intensive care?
options: When his children Dasha and Zakhar arrived from Moscow
When he was allowed to walk outside
When he ate solid food again
reading.correct: When his children Dasha and Zakhar arrived from Moscow
reading.explain: He calls it "самым классным в реанимации" the day his children "Даша и Захар" arrived.

reading.ru: 23 сентября был мой последний день в Шарите.
reading.question: When did Navalny leave the Charité hospital?
reading.correct: September 23
reading.explain: He states "23 сентября был мой последний день в Шарите".

reading.ru: Это была канцлер Германии Ангела Меркель.
reading.question: Who unexpectedly visited Navalny just before his discharge?
reading.correct: German Chancellor Angela Merkel
reading.explain: The mysterious visitor turns out to be "канцлер Германии Ангела Меркель".

reading.ru: Даже помнила название одной из упомянутых там фирм — «Дискурс».
reading.question: What impressed Navalny about Merkel during their conversation?
options: She knew detailed specifics of his corruption investigations
She offered him asylum on the spot
reading.correct: She knew detailed specifics of his corruption investigations
reading.explain: He was impressed that she even remembered a firm's name, «Дискурс», from his investigations.

reading.ru: Я ответил, что хотел бы как можно скорее вернуться в Россию.
reading.question: What did Navalny tell Merkel about his plans?
options: He wanted to return to Russia as soon as possible
He wanted to stay in Germany permanently
He planned to retire from politics
He wanted to move to the United States
reading.correct: He wanted to return to Russia as soon as possible
reading.explain: He told her "я хотел бы как можно скорее вернуться в Россию".

reading.ru: Давай подождем, пока ты восстановишься. Неизвестно, что они решат с тобой сделать опять, когда ты вернешься
reading.question: What did Yulia urge Navalny to do instead of rushing home?
options: Wait until he recovered before returning
reading.correct: Wait until he recovered before returning
reading.explain: Yulia told him "Давай подождем, пока ты восстановишься".

reading.ru: Так мы остались в Германии еще на четыре месяца.
reading.question: How much longer did Navalny end up staying in Germany after being discharged?
reading.correct: Four more months
reading.explain: He concludes "Так мы остались в Германии еще на четыре месяца".
